A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Human Behavior Atlas benchmark and OmniSapiens models. The text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v1 Tables 8–9 to v2 Tables 21–22.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 report original multitask evaluations, held-out transfer experiments and behavioral-descriptor results, including Tables 4–6 and qualitative examples.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, and Appendix D adds transfer experiments, controlled ablations, computational measurements and human–LLM judge agreement results.

M1.justification: The SFT classifier/decoder architecture, pooled-descriptor residual BAM, and GRPO-based generative model remain unchanged in Sections 3.5–3.7 and Appendix B. Added architectural explanations and experimental ablations do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds IEMOCAP as an external emotion-recognition dataset for transfer evaluation. The original 13-dataset, 10-task benchmark remains intact; the other supplementary evaluations principally reuse its datasets.

E2.justification: Table 16 expands transfer comparisons with Gemma-3-4B, HumanOmniV2-7B and untuned Qwen Omni/VL models. Table 20 newly compares RLOO against GRPO, while Table 18 adds Qwen3-30B and human judge comparisons. Table 5's renamed Qwen SFT control was already classifier-equipped in v1 Appendix C.1.

E3.justification: v2 adds zero-shot transfer, adapter and RL configuration sweeps, 500-sample timing and judge-validation protocols, generation-quality metrics and seven-class sentiment reporting. Appendix C.2 changes the reported RL learning rate from 1×10⁻⁶ to 5×10⁻⁷. Main splits remain unchanged; the learning-rate revision does not establish that the main experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's taskwise BAM comparison and qualitative examples, Appendix D adds raw-input removal, descriptor-stream and adapter-width ablations; RL rollout, learning-rate and algorithm comparisons; computational-cost, dataset-imbalance and generation-retention analyses; and judge validation with prompt perturbations.

E5.justification: v2 introduces latency standard deviations across 500 inputs, Spearman correlations and Cohen's kappa estimates in Tables 13, 15 and 18. These expand statistical reporting for supplementary analyses, but neither version reports repeated-training-run counts or confidence intervals for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Tables 4–6 retain their numerical entries, while Appendix D adds substantial results from new evaluations and ablations. Examples include IEMOCAP scores of 0.6213 versus 0.5625 in Table 9 and GPT-5-nano–human agreement of κ=0.78, falling to 0.75 with altered prompts, in Table 18. These are newly reported results rather than same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The BAM equations, SFT objectives, GRPO derivation and reward formulation are retained. Added design explanations and empirical statistical measures introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly describes the model variants as vanilla instances rather than new methods; v2 removes that qualification and calls BAM novel. The principal benchmark, multitask-performance, transfer and targeted-descriptor-benefit claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of late adapter integration and shared behavioral features, plus interpretations concerning descriptor complementarity, adapter capacity, stream selection, imbalance, generation retention and judge reliability. The revised ethics statement also newly asserts that discrimination, bias and fairness issues should not arise, without corresponding analyses.

D1.justification: Where v1 promises release after review, v2 supplies a repository address for the benchmark, models and code. It also adds fresh-session judging instructions, generation-quality and paraphrased judging prompts, timing hardware/precision/batch-size details, and the revised RL learning rate. These substantially expand access and reproduction information.

R1.justification: Five references are added, covering Qwen3-Omni, emotion labeling, language modeling and LLM-based evaluation. BAM's novelty positioning changes from explicitly non-novel supporting variant to novel adapter, while the main related-work discussion and benchmark positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain. v2 changes much 'unified model' terminology to 'foundation model,' expands selected model and transfer explanations, revises contributions and ethics text, updates the conference header, and appends an organized additional-experiments section.

P2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the visual presentation with Tables 8–20 and two additional judging-prompt boxes; some tables reorganize existing scores alongside new comparisons. Figures 1–4 are retained with layout shifts, Table 1 gains a DEP column, and the former appendix Tables 8–9 become Tables 21–22.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked controlled adapter ablations and empirical validation of its LLM judge. v2 adds both, alongside external-dataset and zero-shot transfer evidence, substantially strengthening the empirical foundation. Some new interpretations overreach, particularly claims about negligible imbalance and preserved general generation ability, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the important validation gains.
